C1.rationale: The hard constraints all guard irreversible data loss (stashing a coworker's uncommitted work, force-removing peer worktrees) and each states why — 'committed refs survive, uncommitted does not' — so the model can generalise beyond the enumerated cases; softer guidance is explicitly framed as judgment rather than prohibition. Short of 5 because a few directives are stated as bare imperatives without the reasoning attached (the numbered Response Rules, the 'never auto-clean' anti-pattern row).

C2.rationale: This is a narrative rule file with no arguments, flags, or invocation interface; the parameterised surface belongs to the git-coworker-check skill, not to this unit.

C3.rationale: One file carries everything: the core invariant, six signal implementations as inline bash, a post-corruption recovery table, a Workflow-resume war story, and a limitations list — all resident every turn. It cross-references three sibling rules but splits none of its own rare-path material out, even though a plugin skill with a REFERENCE.md and scripts/ already exists to hold it.

C5.rationale: Primary dimension. A genuine every-turn invariant exists here (treat `git status` as everyone's changes; untracked work has no recovery path), but most of the file is procedure with an explicit trigger — capture a baseline at session start, probe before a destructive op, recover after a bare flip, prune worktrees at cleanup, re-dispatch after a workflow resume — none of which must be resident when the user asked about something else. An on-demand skill (`/git:coworker-check`) already owns exactly that procedure, so the promotion target exists and was not used.

C6.rationale: Runnable artifacts for this exact logic exist and are not named: detect-coworkers.sh, claim-session.sh, release-session.sh, and the tests test_bare_flip.sh / test_worktree_leak.sh. counter_finding: The asymmetry that committed work survives in the reflog while untracked work does not — and the resulting 'treat `git status` as everyone's changes, stage explicit paths' stance — is a true every-turn invariant that no skill trigger would reliably fire on before the damage is done, and it should stay always-loaded.
